headline: Never Forget the One-Pass Hash Map Trick
problem_summary: Given an array and a target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. Exactly one solution exists.
key_insight: For each number, the value needed to reach target is target - num; checking a hash map for that value turns an O(n^2) search into O(1) lookups.
intuition: Walk the array once. For each number, ask a hash map whether its complement has already been seen. If yes, both indices are the answer. If no, record this number's index and keep going.

naive_approach.description: Check every pair of indices with nested loops.

approach: Create an empty hash map from value to index.
For each index i, compute complement = target - nums[i].
If complement is already in the map, return [map[complement], i].
Otherwise store nums[i] -> i in the map and continue.
correctness: Every pair is checked exactly once, either as (complement, current) or (current, complement); the map guarantees the first matching pair found is returned.

complexity.explanation: Single pass with O(1) average hash map operations.
